lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Opens with Elizabeth's early, intimate reassurance that she already understands him.

lines.text: When I opened my door on my return, Flush threw himself upon me with a most ecstatical agony, and for full ten minutes did not cease jumping and kissing my hands—he thought he had lost me for certain, this time.
lines.note: Flush's ecstatic welcome shows the domestic world Robert is entering.

lines.text: Every day shows me more to love in you, dearest, and I open my arms as wide as I can ...
lines.note: Robert's early declaration that every day reveals more to love in her.

lines.text: I have just come from the vestry of Paddington chapel, and bore it very well, and saw nobody except one woman.
lines.note: Elizabeth's small, concrete victory over fear at the chapel.

lines.text: I have lost my poor Flush—lost him!
lines.note: The sudden loss of Flush becomes a shared trial between them.

lines.text: It seems to me that you and I are at one upon the whole question,—only that I am your Flush, and he is mine.
lines.note: Elizabeth's private callback turns Flush into a metaphor for their mutual care.

lines.text: Only a few words to tell you that Flush is found, and lying on the sofa, with one paw and both ears hanging over the edge of it.
lines.note: Flush's recovery brings back one of their recurring figures.

lines.text: I look back, and in every one point, every word and gesture, every letter, every silence—you have been entirely perfect to me—I would not change one word, one look.
lines.note: Robert looks back and finds every word and gesture of hers perfect.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: Elizabeth's breathless report that the wedding day is safely past.

lines.text: What could be better than lifting me from the ground and carrying me into life and the sunshine?
lines.note: Elizabeth credits Robert with lifting her into life and sunshine.

lines.text: I did hate so, to have to take off the ring!
lines.note: The ring she hated to remove marks the new bond they now share openly.

lines.text: Oh—if I loved you less ... a little, little less.
lines.note: Her final, compressed confession that loving him less would make leaving harder.
